title: Story 01: New Feature Request — Full Lifecycle
pmResponse:
# Action Plan: Feature — "Add Search Functionality to the Issue List" ## Scope Analysis This is a **library feature**. Per the scope heuristic, data/API requests involving search, filtering, data models, and business logic belong to the library (the library owns the data layer). The request literally matches the rule's own example: *"Add search to the issue list is a library feature."* No second component (no "screen", "page", or "UI" language) is named, so this is a single-track library deliverable — no webapp involvement, no cross-team coordination. Feature phase flow applies: **Plan → Dev → Validate → Release** (4 phases) + 1 sync tracker = 5 children. --- ## Complete Issue Hierarchy ``` PARENT #1 "Add search functionality to issue list" (tag: feature, assignee: project-manager, status: in-progress) ├── Task #2 "Plan search functionality" (tag: task, assignee: library-architect, status: todo) ├── Task #3 "Develop search functionality" (tag: task, assignee: library-developer, status: todo) ← blocked by #2 ├── Task #4 "Validate search functionality" (tag: task, assignee: library-validator, status: todo) ← blocked by #3 ├── Task #5 "Release search functionality" (tag: task, assignee: library-releaser, status: todo) ← blocked by #4 └── Task #6 "Verify search feature complete" (tag: task,sync, assignee: project-manager, status: todo) ← blocked by #5 ``` --- ## Exact Commands (in execution order) ### Step 1 — Create the parent feature issue ``` agt create "Add search functionality to issue list" \ --tags feature \ --assignee project-manager \ --status todo ``` **Reasoning:** This is a new user-facing capability (searching issues), so the parent tag is `feature`. The parent is assigned to me (project-manager) and starts at `todo` — I flip it to `in-progress` only AFTER all children and blockages are in place (last step). I capture the returned ID as `

`. --- ### Step 2 — Create the Plan phase task ``` agt create "Plan search functionality" \ --tags task \ --assignee library-architect \ --status todo \ --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** Feature planning that involves API/architecture design (how search queries work, what fields are indexed, query interface) goes to the architect. This is the unblocked entry point — the work loop will pick this up first. Captured ID: ``. --- ### Step 3 — Create the Development phase task ``` agt create "Develop search functionality" \ --tags task \ --assignee library-developer \ --status todo \ --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** Implementation from the architect's spec goes to the library-developer. Created now but will be blocked until planning completes. Captured ID: ``. --- ### Step 4 — Create the Validation phase task ``` agt create "Validate search functionality" \ --tags task \ --assignee library-validator \ --status todo \ --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** Validation is ALWAYS a separate task assigned to the team's validator — never the developer who built it. The validator writes tests and performs quality checks. Captured ID: ``. --- ### Step 5 — Create the Release phase task ``` agt create "Release search functionality" \ --tags task \ --assignee library-releaser \ --status todo \ --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** Release is a gate — the releaser runs the full test suite, generates docs, builds, and publishes to npm. If tests fail, release stops and routes back. Captured ID: ``. --- ### Step 6 — Create the sync tracker (the "+1" child) ``` agt create "Verify search feature complete" \ --tags task,sync \ --assignee project-manager \ --status todo \ --parentId

``` **Reasoning:** The sync tracker is my completion alarm. It is a literal extra child with BOTH tags `task,sync` (never just `sync`). It is assigned to me and starts at `todo` — I never set it to `in-progress` myself; the work loop hands it to me when it unblocks. Captured ID: ``. **Child count check:** 4 phase tasks + 1 sync tracker = 5 children. ✓ --- ### Step 7 — Add blockages to sequence the phase chain ``` agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** Development cannot start until the plan/spec exists. ``` agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** Validation cannot start until implementation is complete. ``` agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** Release cannot proceed until validation passes. ``` agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** The sync tracker is blocked by the **last worker child** (Release). While Release is `todo`/`in-progress`, the sync tracker stays blocked and the loop skips it — I am not bothered. When the releaser marks Release `done`, auto-clear unblocks the sync tracker → the loop hands it to me → I verify and close the feature. --- ### Step 8 — Flip the parent to in-progress (LAST action) ``` agt update

--status in-progress ``` **Reasoning:** The parent must be set to `in-progress` immediately after creating children. This prevents the work loop from re-waking me every cycle on the same parent. This is done **last** — after all children and blockages exist — so the structure is complete before the loop sees an active parent. --- ### Step 9 — Add a context comment to the parent ``` agt comments add

--content "Library feature: search functionality for the issue list. Phases: Plan (library-architect) → Dev (library-developer) → Validate (library-validator) → Release (library-releaser). Scope is library-only — no webapp/UI changes in this deliverable. Sync tracker will fire when release completes." ``` **Reasoning:** Documents the plan and scope decision for traceability. Makes it clear to any reviewer why only the library sub-team is involved and why no webapp track exists. --- ## What Happens Next (I do nothing further) After step 8, I step back. The work loop takes over: 1. `` is `todo`, assigned to `library-architect`, has no open blockages → loop wakes the architect → they set `in-progress`, design the search API, comment with the spec, mark `done`. 2. Auto-clear resolves ``'s blockage → loop wakes `library-developer` → implements → `done`. 3. Auto-clear unblocks `` → `library-validator` tests → `done`. 4. Auto-clear unblocks `` → `library-releaser` builds/publishes → `done`. 5. Auto-clear unblocks `` → loop hands it to **me** → I verify the release, mark `` `done`, then mark `

` `done`. No manual blockage resolution in the work loop — auto-clear drives the chain.
feedback: Excellent response. Correct 5-child hierarchy (4 phase tasks + 1 sync tracker) under a feature parent with proper tags. Assignments map perfectly to phase-to-agent (architect/developer/validator/releaser/PM). Sequential blockage chain (DEV<-PLAN, VAL<-DEV, REL<-VAL, SYNC<-REL) with sync tracker correctly assigned to PM and blocked by last worker child. Parent created in todo then flipped to in-progress as the final action after all children/blockages exist. Sync tracker carries both task,sync tags. All key behaviors and commands fully covered with sound reasoning.
